---
title: "Research"
---

I am interested in how cells decide when, where and how strongly to express their
genes, with a focus on plants. Most of my work is about transcription: how
regulatory DNA and chromatin determine where it begins and how much of it occurs,
and how this changes during development and in response to the environment. I
combine genome-wide assays and genetics with computational models of regulatory
sequence.

## Transcription initiation and enhancers

Much of what a promoter does is visible only at the level of transcription start
sites. Using csRNA-seq, which captures nascent initiation events directly, I showed
that divergent and non-coding transcription is an active part of gene regulation
during the *Arabidopsis* seed-to-seedling transition, validated it
genetically, and found that active plant enhancers are transcribed
into enhancer RNAs, as in animals
([Nature Communications, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46082-5)).

Because active enhancers are transcribed, csRNA-seq finds them genome-wide,
including many that chromatin accessibility alone misses. I am using it
to identify *Arabidopsis* enhancers during development and to link them to the genes
they control. I am also taking these approaches beyond plants: with collaborators, I
am profiling transcription initiation in the algal and fungal partners of lichens,
building on our work on transposable element diversification in lichen symbionts
([bioRxiv, 2026](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.14.705750)). During my PhD I also
led the bioinformatics for a multi-laboratory study of how *Arabidopsis*
transcription changes as autumn progresses into winter under simulated field
temperatures ([Genome Biology, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-026-04289-3)).

## Plant immunity

At The Sainsbury Laboratory I study how plant cells switch on immune responses. I
combine a csRNA-seq time course with single-nucleus RNA and ATAC multiomics of
*Arabidopsis* seedlings treated with flg22, a bacterial elicitor of pattern-triggered
immunity, to map the enhancers that immunity activates, connect them to their target
genes and resolve how each cell type responds. So far the mesophyll mounts the
strongest early defence response, and early and later cell type-specific responses
appear to be driven largely by the same WRKY transcription factors (posters from
[2025](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21476383) and
[2026](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21476601)).

![Single-nucleus multiome profiles of 25,728 nuclei from *Arabidopsis* seedlings,
coloured by cell type. From Tremblay, Pai and Nobori, poster at Plant Biology 2026
([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)).](images/research/immunity.png){width=50% fig-align="center" fig-alt="UMAP of Arabidopsis seedling nuclei clustered into mesophyll, epidermis, vascular, root and other cell types"}

## Models of regulatory sequence

I train and interpret deep sequence-to-function models of chromatin accessibility
and transcription initiation, and use them to ask which sequence features explain
regulatory activity. At The Sainsbury Laboratory I have trained models from scratch
and fine-tuned ChromBPNet and seq2PRINT on single-cell ATAC-seq data from about
30,000 flg22-treated *Arabidopsis* cells, evaluating their accuracy and biases and
interpreting their predictions with attribution and feature ablation. This builds on my long-running work on sequence motifs and the
[universalmotif](software.qmd) package.

![A contribution-weight logo of a CACGTG motif, in which bases can contribute
positively or negatively, drawn with universalmotif.](images/research/motif.png){fig-alt="Sequence logo with positive and negative base contributions around a CACGTG motif"}

## Earlier work

For my MSc I studied what happens when plants cannot efficiently recycle
methylthioadenosine (MTA): it builds up in reproductive tissues, disrupts sulfur
assimilation and lowers fertility
([Journal of Experimental Botany, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/erag135)).
Between my MSc and PhD I worked on the comparative genomics of bacterial pathogens,
including the phylogenomics of 8,839 *Clostridioides difficile* genomes
([PLOS Pathogens, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1009181)), phylogenetic
profiling of bacterial gene function
([Bioinformatics, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa1105)), and studies
of *C. difficile* toxin B receptors
([Nature Communications, 2022](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-33964-9)) and
ancient tetanus neurotoxins
([Nature Communications, 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-41174-0)). During
the COVID-19 pandemic I worked with clinicians and virologists on SARS-CoV-2,
predicting its recombination potential
([Journal of General Virology, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1099/jgv.0.001491)) and
profiling viral receptors and interferon responses in human airway epithelium
([European Respiratory Journal, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1183/13993003.01123-2020);
[iScience, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2021.102477)).
